newsitem.title: UK: UK unleaded petrol margins tighten - analyst.
newsitem.headline: UK unleaded petrol margins tighten - analyst.

text.p: Retail margins for unleaded petrol (gasoline) in the U.K. tightened in January and February versus late 1996, dashing hopes for a swift recovery in the ferocious petrol market, according to independent analysts Oil Price Assessments Ltd (OPAL).
But margins for auto diesel staged a recovery in February after a sharp drop in spot gas oil prices outpaced a drop in prices at the pump, said Peter Regnier, director of OPAL.
"It just seems that prices are eroding progressively, possibly pulled down by the supermarkets," Regnier said. "The supermarkets seem to be quite aggressive at the moment."
Gross margins on unleaded gasoline for major brand operators narrowed to 4.7 pence per litre in mid-February, versus 5.0 in January and 5.3 in December, Regnier said.

He said margins of 4.7 pence per litre were obviously better than at the height of the price war last year, but were still "totally inadequate" for many operators needing margins of 6-7 pence to be profitable.
"Yes, it is better than the extreme of the price war but it still isn't glorious," he said.
The 1996 average for unleaded gasoline was 3.7 pence per litre and for auto diesel 3.6 pence, he said.
The current average pump price in the U.K. for 95 unleaded is 60.2 pence per litre, versus 60.8 pence in January and 61.2 pence in December, he said.
But there are wide variations, with prices as low as 55 pence per litre in some areas that were being offered by Esso, he said.
Esso, as part of its Pricewatch campaign launched a year ago, promises to match the lowest prices in its markets.
Auto diesel margins recovered to 5.0 pence per litre in mid-February from 4.2 in January and 4.6 in December, he said.
